subject: Request: Conditional Overage Credit + Packaging Amendment — VP/CFO signoff needed
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request signoff: proposed conditional overage credit + packaging amendment for Astrawell

Team —

Quick summary: Astrawell (pilot -> enterprise conversion) asked for two nonstandard asks that materially change economics: 1) a 3-month "surge protection" overage credit (they want overage billed at 0.5x our published overage rate for spikes above committed threshold for months 1–3 post-go-live) and 2) a packaging swap: move from a per-seat/per-token pilot pricing to a concurrency-based license with a 12-month minimum commit (they want the flexibility to burst but with a lower base).

Why this matters: combined, the asks reduce first-year unit revenue by ~21% vs our standard ramp schedule (see attached cost-model-appendix.xlsx). Motive from Astrawell: predictable monthly invoice when usage spikes during clinical trials; they argue this reduces churn risk and accelerates adoption across regions.

Recommended escalation/approval ask: we think this can be approved with VP/CFO signoff if we: 
- Limit the 0.5x overage credit to three discrete calendar months and a single contiguous surge window (no rolling application).
- Require written notice 7 days before anticipated surge if possible (they said ops can give heads-up).
- Add a one-time implementation fee ($25k) and a success milestone credit structure (50% of implementation fee is refundable if they hit 90%+ of projected committed usage by month 6).
- Tie the concurrency packaging change to a 12-month minimum payment commitment and a clause that reverts to standard per-token terms if they terminate early (pro-rated clawback).

Please see attached draft amendment (draft-amendment-Astrawell.docx) and the P&L impact tab in the workbook. I need an explicit VP/CFO approval string we can paste to Astrawell legal if you approve.

Request: Kimberly — any chance you can weigh in on tolerance for the short-term margin hit? Aditya/Marissa — are you comfortable operationally with the notice + milestone approach?

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Astrawell_MA_plan_v2.pdf (proposal), cost-model-appendix.xlsx (sensitivity analysis), draft-amendment-Astrawell.docx (redline)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T14:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request signoff: proposed conditional overage credit + packaging amendment for Astrawell

Kimberly — forwarding Rishi's note with my suggested simplifications to reduce operational burden.

Key changes I recommend before we present to Finance/CFO:
- Replace 7-day notice with a soft "forecast window" (they need to give a 72-hour heads-up where possible) — operations prefers this for scheduling capacity.
- Cap the total discounted overage liability at $45k per surge window to bound downside.
- Convert the refundable implementation fee to milestone credits applied to subsequent invoices rather than refunds — keeps billing simpler.

I've spoken to Jacob Stern (procurement at Astrawell) — they're flexible on the payment mechanics but want the 3-month credit to be explicit in contract to reassure internal sponsors. Jacob asked for a one-line approval from our CFO to attach to their procurement packet.

If Kimberly is OK with the cap + credit mechanics, Rishi can share the proposed one-liner for signature.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request signoff: proposed conditional overage credit + packaging amendment for Astrawell

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. I've reviewed the cost model and have three quick questions before signoff: 
1) How likely is Astrawell to trigger >1 surge window in the first 12 months? If it's frequent the $45k cap won't be enough.
2) Who owns monitoring/validation of the surge window (our infra team or their ops)? We need a deterministic measurement to avoid disputes.
3) Confirm whether the concurrency license can be invoiced on a monthly true-up rather than an unpredictably timed invoice (finance prefers monthly cadence).

Assuming: single surge window (most likely), monitoring by Redwood with an agreed telemetry export, and monthly true-ups, I'm comfortable approving the conditional credit limited to three months and the packaging swap with the 12-month commit. Approval string below is acceptable for procurement. Please ensure legal inserts the cap clause and the clawback language.

Approval string for procurement: 
"Redwood Inference (Finance) approves a one-time conditional overage credit for Astrawell Health limited to a single surge window up to three consecutive months, with a capped total liability of $45,000, conditional on a 12-month minimum concurrency commitment and the attached milestone credit mechanics. This approval is provided for the explicit deal DL-2026-0347 and must be reflected in the executed amendment. — Kimberly Park, VP Finance, Redwood Inference"

Marissa/Rishi — please confirm operational ownership and I will sign once legal has the amended language.

Kimberly Park
VP, Finance & Operations
Redwood Inference

Jacob / Astrawell team —

Thank you for the flexibility in our discussions. Per attached draft amendment and finance signoff below, Redwood can approve the conditional surge protection structure for DL-2026-0347. Finance has provided the following approval statement for your procurement packet (to be incorporated into the amendment):

"Redwood Inference (Finance) approves a one-time conditional overage credit for Astrawell Health limited to a single surge window up to three consecutive months, with a capped total liability of $45,000, conditional on a 12-month minimum concurrency commitment and the attached milestone credit mechanics. This approval is provided for the explicit deal DL-2026-0347 and must be reflected in the executed amendment. — Kimberly Park, VP Finance, Redwood Inference"

Operational notes: 
- Redwood will own surge validation (we will push a telemetry export to Astrawell and publish the validation report within 72 hours after a flagged window).
- Invoicing will be monthly with a true-up for concurrency usage (monthly cadence so Astrawell control budget cycles).
- Implementation fee of $25,000 will be applied as milestone credits: 50% of the fee is credited back over months 4–6 conditional on usage targets (details in amendment).

Next steps: Astrawell legal to incorporate the cap, clawback and telemetry clause; once we have a redline we can circulate for signing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
